issues.legal_issue: An abettor’s liability for instigating an offence is not extinguished merely because the person instigated is acquitted, but liability for abetment on the basis that the offence was committed in consequence of the abetment requires proof of that connection.
material_facts: The appellant was found to have instigated a co-accused to set fire to a hut.
The co-accused was acquitted of setting fire to the hut, and the courts found that he had not done so.
Although the hut was set on fire by someone, there was no finding that the person who set it on fire participated in the incident with the appellant or acted at his instigation.
The High Court’s finding that the appellant had instigated the co-accused was maintained.
issues.conclusion: The conviction for abetment on the basis that the offence was committed in consequence of the abetment could not stand because the required causal connection was not established. The appellant remained guilty of abetting the offence by instigation even though the instigated person did not commit it, so the conviction was altered to abetment of an uncompleted offence and the sentence was reduced.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 107 and 108 of the Indian Penal Code, abetment may occur through instigation, conspiracy, or intentional aid, and the abetted act need not be committed for abetment by instigation or conspiracy to be complete. Section 109 applies when the act is committed in consequence of the abetment; section 115 provides punishment for abetting an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life when that offence is not committed in consequence of the abetment. The Court relied on Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. The King Emperor and Faguna Kanta Nath v. The State of Assam, and distinguished Gallu Sah v. The State of Bihar, where the findings supported that a member of the unlawful assembly had acted in consequence of the appellant’s instigation. Where the alleged abetment is intentional aid, acquittal of the alleged principal may defeat the charge if the underlying offence is not established.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_abettor_convicti: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction for abetting an offence.
predicates.appellant_instigated_another_to_commit_o: The appellant instigated another person to commit the offence.
predicates.instigated_person_did_not_commit_offence: The person who was instigated did not commit the offence.
predicates.another_person_committed_act_without_fin: Another person committed the relevant act, but the courts made no finding that this person acted in consequence of the appellant’s instigation.

issues.definition: When an appellant convicted as an abettor instigated a person who did not commit the offence, and another person’s act was not found to result from that instigation, the consequence-based abetment conviction is replaced with a conviction for abetting an offence that was not committed in consequence of the abetment.
